subproblem.title: Convex-combination substitution bound on a ball
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every measurable h : ℝ^n → [0, ∞], every r > 0 and every t ∈ [0, 1], with B_r = ball(0, r) and Lebesgue measure |·|: ∫⁻_{x ∈ B_r} ∫⁻_{y ∈ B_r} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dy dx ≤ 2^n · |B_r| · ∫⁻_{B_r} h (outer variable x, inner variable y; lintegrals in [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Rn n → ℝ≥0∞), Measurable h → ∀ r t : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ∫⁻ y in ball (0 : Rn n) r, h ((1 - t) • y + t • x) ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * volume (ball (0 : Rn n) r) * ∫⁻ z in ball (0 : Rn n) r, h z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 1 of the parent proof (the two substitution cases 1/2 ≤ t < 1 and 0 < t ≤ 1/2, with Jacobians t^n and (1 − t)^n ≥ 2^{−n}), isolated for an arbitrary measurable h ≥ 0 and an arbitrary radius r > 0, and covering the endpoints t = 0, 1.

Notation. B := B_r = ball(0, r) ⊆ Rn n; |·| is Lebesgue measure (volume); 1_B h is the indicator (h on B, 0 off B); all integrals are lintegrals in [0, ∞].

Proof.
1. Affine change of variables. For every measurable F : ℝ^n → [0, ∞], c ∈ ℝ^n and s ≠ 0: ∫ F(c + s·x) dx = ENNReal.ofReal |(s^n)^{−1}| · ∫ F(z) dz. Indeed x ↦ s·x is measurable and Measure.map_addHaar_smul gives map(x ↦ s·x)(Lebesgue) = ENNReal.ofReal |(s^{finrank})^{−1}| · Lebesgue with finrank ℝ (Rn n) = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). By lintegral_map (z ↦ F(c + z) is measurable) and lintegral_smul_measure, ∫ F(c + s·x) dx = ENNReal.ofReal |(s^n)^{−1}| · ∫ F(c + z) dz, and ∫ F(c + z) dz = ∫ F (translation invariance, lintegral_add_left_eq_self).
2. Convexity. For x, y ∈ B and t ∈ [0,1], (1 − t)·y + t·x ∈ B (convex_ball; indeed |(1 − t)y + tx| ≤ (1 − t)|y| + t|x| < r).
3. Key bound. Let c ∈ ℝ^n and s ≥ 1/2 be such that c + s·x ∈ B for every x ∈ B. Then ∫_{x ∈ B} h(c + s·x) dx ≤ 2^n ∫_B h. Proof: for x ∈ B, h(c + s·x) = (1_B h)(c + s·x) (setLIntegral_congr_fun), so ∫_B h(c + s·x) dx = ∫_B (1_B h)(c + s·x) dx ≤ ∫_{ℝ^n} (1_B h)(c + s·x) dx (setLIntegral_le_lintegral) = ENNReal.ofReal |(s^n)^{−1}| · ∫ 1_B h (step 1; 1_B h is measurable and s ≠ 0) = ENNReal.ofReal |(s^n)^{−1}| · ∫_B h (lintegral_indicator). Finally |(s^n)^{−1}| = (s^{−1})^n ≤ 2^n because 0 < s^{−1} ≤ 2 (pow_le_pow_left₀), and ENNReal.ofReal(2^n) = 2^n.
4. Measurability. (x, y) ↦ h((1 − t)·y + t·x) is measurable on ℝ^n × ℝ^n (h measurable, the map continuous).
5. Case t ≥ 1/2. By Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap; restricted Lebesgue measures are s-finite; step 4), LHS = ∫_{y ∈ B} ∫_{x ∈ B} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dx dy. For y ∈ B apply step 3 with c := (1 − t)·y and s := t ≥ 1/2 (c + t·x ∈ B for x ∈ B by step 2): the inner integral is ≤ 2^n ∫_B h. Hence (setLIntegral_mono') LHS ≤ ∫_{y ∈ B} 2^n ∫_B h dy = 2^n |B| ∫_B h (setLIntegral_const).
6. Case t < 1/2. For x ∈ B rewrite (1 − t)·y + t·x = t·x + (1 − t)·y and apply step 3 with c := t·x and s := 1 − t > 1/2 (c + s·y ∈ B for y ∈ B by step 2): ∫_{y ∈ B} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dy ≤ 2^n ∫_B h. Integrating over x ∈ B (setLIntegral_mono', setLIntegral_const): LHS ≤ 2^n |B| ∫_B h.
7. Every t ∈ [0,1] falls under case 5 or case 6, so ∫_{B_r}∫_{B_r} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dy dx ≤ 2^n |B_r| ∫_{B_r} h. ∎

theorem poincare_ball_convex_combination_bound : ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Rn n → ℝ≥0∞), Measurable h → ∀ r t : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ∫⁻ y in ball (0 : Rn n) r, h ((1 - t) • y + t • x) ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * volume (ball (0 : Rn n) r) * ∫⁻ z in ball (0 : Rn n) r, h z := by
  intro n h hh r t hr ht0 ht1
  set B := ball (0 : Rn n) r with hB
  -- 1. affine change of variables: ∫ F(c + s x) dx = |s|^{-n} ∫ F
  have affine : ∀ (F : Rn n → ℝ≥0∞), Measurable F → ∀ (c : Rn n) {s : ℝ}, s ≠ 0 →
      ∫⁻ x, F (c + s • x) = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z, F z := by
    intro F hF c s hs
    have hm : Measurable (fun z : Rn n => F (c + z)) := hF.comp (measurable_const_add c)
    have hmap := lintegral_map (μ := (volume : Measure (Rn n))) hm
      (measurable_const_smul s : Measurable fun x : Rn n => s • x)
    rw [← hmap, Measure.map_addHaar_smul volume hs, lintegral_smul_measure,
      lintegral_add_left_eq_self (μ := (volume : Measure (Rn n))) F c, smul_eq_mul,
      finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]
  -- 2. convexity of the ball
  have hmem : ∀ x ∈ B, ∀ y ∈ B, (1 - t) • y + t • x ∈ B := fun x hx y hy =>
    convex_ball (0 : Rn n) r hy hx (by linarith) ht0 (by ring)
  -- 3. one-variable bound when the coefficient of the integration variable is ≥ 1/2
  have key : ∀ (c : Rn n) (s : ℝ), 1 / 2 ≤ s → (∀ x ∈ B, c + s • x ∈ B) →
      ∫⁻ x in B, h (c + s • x) ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
    intro c s hs hcs
    have hs' : 0 < s := by linarith
    calc ∫⁻ x in B, h (c + s • x) = ∫⁻ x in B, B.indicator h (c + s • x) := by
          refine setLIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_ball (fun x hx => ?_)
          rw [indicator_of_mem (hcs x hx)]
      _ ≤ ∫⁻ x, B.indicator h (c + s • x) := setLIntegral_le_lintegral _ _
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z, B.indicator h z :=
          affine _ (hh.indicator measurableSet_ball) c hs'.ne'
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
          rw [lintegral_indicator measurableSet_ball]
      _ ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
          gcongr
          have h1 : |(s ^ n)⁻¹| ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ n := by
            rw [abs_of_pos (by positivity), ← inv_pow]
            exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (by positivity) (inv_le_of_inv_le₀ (by norm_num) (by linarith)) n
          calc ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((2 : ℝ) ^ n) := ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal h1
            _ = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n := by rw [ENNReal.ofReal_pow (by norm_num)]; simp
  have hH : Measurable (fun p : Rn n × Rn n => h ((1 - t) • p.2 + t • p.1)) :=
    hh.comp (by fun_prop : Continuous fun p : Rn n × Rn n => (1 - t) • p.2 + t • p.1).measurable
  rcases le_or_gt (1 / 2 : ℝ) t with ht | ht
  · -- 4. t ≥ 1/2: Tonelli, then substitute in x
    rw [lintegral_lintegral_swap hH.aemeasurable]
    calc ∫⁻ y in B, ∫⁻ x in B, h ((1 - t) • y + t • x)
        ≤ ∫⁻ y in B, (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
          refine setLIntegral_mono' measurableSet_ball fun y hy => ?_
          exact key ((1 - t) • y) t ht (fun x hx => hmem x hx y hy)
      _ = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * volume B * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
          rw [setLIntegral_const]; ring
  · -- 5. t < 1/2: substitute in y directly
    calc ∫⁻ x in B, ∫⁻ y in B, h ((1 - t) • y + t • x)
        ≤ ∫⁻ x in B, (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
          refine setLIntegral_mono' measurableSet_ball fun x hx => ?_
          have e : ∀ y : Rn n, (1 - t) • y + t • x = t • x + (1 - t) • y := fun y => add_comm _ _
          simp_rw [e]
          exact key (t • x) (1 - t) (by linarith) (fun y hy => by rw [← e]; exact hmem x hx y hy)
      _ = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ n * volume B * ∫⁻ z in B, h z := by
          rw [setLIntegral_const]; ring

proof_key_steps: Affine change of variables ∫ F(c + s x) dx = |s^n|^{-1} ∫ F via Measure.map_addHaar_smul, lintegral_map and translation invariance
Convexity: (1 − t)y + tx ∈ B_r for x, y ∈ B_r
Key bound: if s ≥ 1/2 and c + sB ⊆ B then ∫_B h(c + s x) dx ≤ 2^n ∫_B h (replace h by 1_B h, extend to ℝ^n, substitute)
Case t ≥ 1/2: Tonelli, then key bound in x for each y
Case t < 1/2: key bound in y for each x
Integrate the constant bound over the outer ball to get 2^n |B_r| ∫_{B_r} h

      lintegral_congr_ae (h.mono fun y hy => by simp [hy])
    simp_rw [h1]

  have hff' := hf.ae_eq_mk
  have hm : StronglyMeasurable (hf.mk f) := hf.stronglyMeasurable_mk
  set f' := hf.mk f
  -- 1. radii r_m = 1 - 1/(m+2) ↑ 1
  let r : ℕ → ℝ := fun m => 1 - 1 / ((m : ℝ) + 2)
  have hr0 : ∀ m, 0 < r m := fun m => by
    have : (1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 2) < 1 := by
      rw [div_lt_one (by positivity)]; linarith [(Nat.cast_nonneg m : (0:ℝ) ≤ m)]
    simp only [r]; linarith
  have hr1 : ∀ m, r m < 1 := fun m => by
    have : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / ((m : ℝ) + 2) := by positivity
    simp only [r]; linarith
  have hrmono : Monotone r := by
    intro a b hab
    simp only [r]
    have hab' : (a : ℝ) + 2 ≤ (b : ℝ) + 2 := by exact_mod_cast Nat.add_le_add_right hab 2
    have : (1 : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) + 2) ≤ 1 / ((a : ℝ) + 2) :=
      one_div_le_one_div_of_le (by positivity) hab'
    linarith
  set B : ℕ → Set (Rn n) := fun m => ball 0 (r m) with hBdef
  have hBmono : Monotone B := fun a b hab => ball_subset_ball (hrmono hab)

    ext x

        rw [div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]
        rw [div_lt_iff₀ h1] at hm
        nlinarith [(Nat.cast_nonneg m : (0:ℝ) ≤ m)]
      linarith

  have hK' : ∀ m, ∫⁻ x in B m, ∫⁻ y in B m, ‖f' x - f' y‖ₑ ^ 2 ≤ K := fun m => by
    rw [← dbl (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset (ball_subset_ball (hr1 m).le) hff')]

subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every C^1 function φ : ℝ^n → ℝ and every r with 0 < r ≤ 1: ∫⁻_{x ∈ B_r} ∫⁻_{y ∈ B_r} ‖φ(x) − φ(y)‖ₑ² dy dx ≤ 2^{n+2} · |B_1| · ∫⁻_{B_r} ‖∇φ‖ₑ², where B_s = ball(0, s), |B_1| is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball and ∇φ is Mathlib's gradient φ (lintegrals in [0, ∞]).

Notation. B := B_r = ball(0, r), B_1 = ball(0, 1); |·| is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n and λ Lebesgue measure on ℝ; all integrals are lintegrals in [0, ∞].

Proof.
1. Regularity. φ is C^1, so Dφ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, 1 ≠ 0) and ∇φ = toDual⁻¹ ∘ Dφ is continuous. Hence h(z) := ‖∇φ(z)‖ₑ² is measurable, and (x, y, t) ↦ h((1 − t)·y + t·x) is measurable both as a function on (ℝ^n × ℝ^n) × ℝ and as a function on (ℝ^n × ℝ) × ℝ^n (a measurable function composed with continuous maps).
2. Pointwise bound. Let x, y ∈ B. Then |x − y| ≤ |x| + |y| < 2r ≤ 2, so ‖x − y‖ₑ² ≤ 4, and by sibling (1): ‖φ(x) − φ(y)‖ₑ² ≤ ‖x − y‖ₑ² ∫⁻_{[0,1]} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dt ≤ 4 ∫⁻_{[0,1]} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dt.
3. Integrating step 2 over y ∈ B and then over x ∈ B (setLIntegral_mono') and pulling out the constant 4 (lintegral_const_mul', twice): ∫_B∫_B ‖φ(x) − φ(y)‖ₑ² dy dx ≤ 4 ∫_{x ∈ B}∫_{y ∈ B}∫_{t ∈ [0,1]} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dt dy dx.
4. Tonelli. For each fixed x swap the y- and t-integrals (lintegral_lintegral_swap, measurability from step 1); then swap the x- and t-integrals (lintegral_lintegral_swap, using that (x, t) ↦ ∫_{y ∈ B} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dy is measurable by Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'). Thus the triple integral equals ∫_{t ∈ [0,1]} (∫_{x ∈ B}∫_{y ∈ B} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dy dx) dt.
5. For every t ∈ [0,1], sibling (2) applied to the measurable h, the radius r > 0 and t gives ∫_{x ∈ B}∫_{y ∈ B} h((1 − t)·y + t·x) dy dx ≤ 2^n |B| ∫_B h. Integrating over t ∈ [0,1] (setLIntegral_mono') and using λ([0,1]) = 1 (setLIntegral_const, Real.volume_Icc), the t-integral is ≤ 2^n |B| ∫_B h.

subproblem.title: Double-integral estimate for L²-limits of C^1 approximations on B_r
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, 0 < r ≤ 1, f : ℝ^n → ℝ and g : ℝ^n → ℝ^n be a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to B_r = ball(0, r), and let φ_j : ℝ^n → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) be C^1 functions such that ∫⁻_{B_r} ‖φ_j − f‖ₑ² → 0 and ∫⁻_{B_r} ‖∇φ_j − g‖ₑ² → 0 as j → ∞. Then ∫⁻_{x ∈ B_r} ∫⁻_{y ∈ B_r} ‖f(x) − f(y)‖ₑ² dy dx ≤ 2^{n+2} · |B_1| · ∫⁻_{B_r} ‖g‖ₑ², where |B_1| is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball (lintegrals in [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (g : Rn n → Rn n) (φ : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → AEStronglyMeasurable f (volume.restrict (ball (0 : Rn n) r)) → AEStronglyMeasurable g (volume.restrict (ball (0 : Rn n) r)) → (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (φ j)) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ‖φ j x - f x‖ₑ ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun j => ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ‖gradient (φ j) x - g x‖ₑ ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 0) → ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ∫⁻ y in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ‖f x - f y‖ₑ ^ 2 ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (n + 2) * volume (ball (0 : Rn n) 1) * ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ‖g x‖ₑ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 2 of the parent proof ('Passage to f on B_r': Minkowski, an a.e.-convergent subsequence, Fatou first in y and then in x), stated for an arbitrary approximating sequence of the form produced by the uncle lemma Submission.w12_ball_smooth_approximation, so that this lemma itself only needs the sibling (3) Submission.poincare_c1_ball_double_integral_bound (key smooth_estimate). The measurability hypothesis on g is essential (lintegrals of non-measurable functions are lower integrals).

Notation. B := B_r; μ := Lebesgue measure restricted to B (a finite measure); C := 2^{n+2}|B_1|, which is finite since |B_1| < ∞; ‖u‖_2 := eLpNorm u 2 μ. For a.e.-strongly measurable u, ‖u‖_2 = (∫‖u‖ₑ² dμ)^{1/2} (eLpNorm_eq_lintegral_rpow_enorm_toReal), hence ‖u‖_2² = ∫‖u‖ₑ² dμ, and if ∫‖u_j‖ₑ² dμ → 0 then ‖u_j‖_2 → 0 (continuity of a ↦ a^{1/2} on [0, ∞] and 0^{1/2} = 0).

Proof.
0. Representative. Let f' be strongly measurable with f = f' μ-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). Then ∫_B∫_B ‖f(x) − f(y)‖ₑ² = ∫_B∫_B ‖f'(x) − f'(y)‖ₑ²: for each x the inner integrands agree μ-a.e. in y, and then the outer integrands agree μ-a.e. in x (lintegral_congr_ae twice). Likewise ∫_B ‖φ_j − f'‖ₑ² = ∫_B ‖φ_j − f‖ₑ² → 0. So it suffices to prove the claim for f'.
1. Regularity. Each φ_j is continuous and ∇φ_j = toDual⁻¹ ∘ Dφ_j is continuous (φ_j is C^1).
2. A.e.-convergent subsequence. ‖φ_j − f'‖_2 → 0, hence φ_j → f' in μ-measure (tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_eLpNorm with p = 2 ≠ 0), and there is a strictly increasing ns : ℕ → ℕ with φ_{ns(i)}(x) → f'(x) for μ-a.e. x (TendstoInMeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae).
3. Inner Fatou. Fix x at which the convergence of step 2 holds (this is μ-a.e. x). For μ-a.e. y the convergence holds at y too; by continuity of (a, b) ↦ ‖a − b‖ₑ² : ℝ × ℝ → [0, ∞], ‖φ_{ns i}(x) − φ_{ns i}(y)‖ₑ² → ‖f'(x) − f'(y)‖ₑ², so ‖f'(x) − f'(y)‖ₑ² = liminf_i ‖φ_{ns i}(x) − φ_{ns i}(y)‖ₑ² (Tendsto.liminf_eq). By lintegral_congr_ae and Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le; each y ↦ ‖φ_{ns i}(x) − φ_{ns i}(y)‖ₑ² is measurable): ∫_B ‖f'(x) − f'(y)‖ₑ² dy ≤ liminf_i G_i(x), where G_i(x) := ∫_B ‖φ_{ns i}(x) − φ_{ns i}(y)‖ₑ² dy.
4. Outer Fatou. Each G_i is measurable (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right', the integrand being measurable on ℝ^n × ℝ^n). By step 3 (μ-a.e. in x; lintegral_mono_ae) and Fatou again: ∫_B∫_B ‖f'(x) − f'(y)‖ₑ² ≤ ∫_B liminf_i G_i ≤ liminf_i ∫_B G_i = liminf_i D_i, with D_i := ∫_B∫_B ‖φ_{ns i}(x) − φ_{ns i}(y)‖ₑ² dy dx.
5. Smooth estimate and Minkowski. By sibling (3) (φ_{ns i} is C^1 and 0 < r ≤ 1): D_i ≤ C ∫_B ‖∇φ_{ns i}‖ₑ² = C ‖∇φ_{ns i}‖_2². Writing ∇φ_{ns i} = g + (∇φ_{ns i} − g), Minkowski's inequality in L²(μ) (eLpNorm_add_le, 1 ≤ 2) gives ‖∇φ_{ns i}‖_2 ≤ ‖g‖_2 + ε_i with ε_i := ‖∇φ_{ns i} − g‖_2. Hence D_i ≤ C (‖g‖_2 + ε_i)².
6. Limit. Since ∇φ_j − g is a.e.-strongly measurable and ∫_B ‖∇φ_j − g‖ₑ² → 0, we get ‖∇φ_j − g‖_2 → 0, so ε_i → 0 (composition with ns, which tends to ∞; StrictMono.tendsto_atTop). By continuity of addition and squaring on [0, ∞] and of multiplication by the finite constant C (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul), C(‖g‖_2 + ε_i)² → C‖g‖_2².
7. Conclusion. ∫_B∫_B ‖f'(x) − f'(y)‖ₑ² ≤ liminf_i D_i ≤ liminf_i C(‖g‖_2 + ε_i)² (liminf_le_liminf) = C‖g‖_2² (Tendsto.liminf_eq) = C ∫_B ‖g‖ₑ² = 2^{n+2} |B_1| ∫_{B_r} ‖g‖ₑ². All steps are valid in [0, ∞], including the case ∫_{B_r} ‖g‖ₑ² = ∞. ∎
